objective.statement: Recognise and name the trill, turn, upper and lower mordent, acciaccatura and appoggiatura.
successCriteria: I know the signs that go above a note.
I know the small notes that go before a note.
I know ornaments take no time in the bar.

explanation.text: Composers decorate notes with ornaments. They are written in two ways: by small notes just before the main note, or by special signs above the stave. Neither takes any time in the bar: the time values of the full-size notes add up exactly as if the small notes and signs were not there.

music.textAlternative: A bar of four minims on E, each with a sign above it: a trill, a turn, an upper mordent and a lower mordent.

explanation.caption: Signs above a note: trill (tr), turn, upper mordent, lower mordent.

explanation.text: The trill is written tr, sometimes followed by a wavy line. The turn is a sideways S-shaped curl. The mordent is a short zig-zag: with no line through it, it is the upper mordent; with a short vertical line through it, it is the lower mordent.

music.textAlternative: A bar of two minims on E: the first with a small crushed note before it, the second with a small note before it.

explanation.caption: Small notes before the main note: acciaccatura (with a stroke), appoggiatura (without).

explanation.text: A small note with a diagonal stroke through its stem and flag is an acciaccatura (a 'crushed' note). A small note with no stroke is an appoggiatura. At Grade 4 you need to recognise and name all six; how each is played is a Grade 5 topic.
Signs above: tr = trill, curl = turn, zig-zag = upper mordent, zig-zag with a line = lower mordent. Small notes: stroke = acciaccatura, no stroke = appoggiatura. None counts in the bar.

music.textAlternative: A bar of two minims on G, the first with a trill sign, the second with a turn sign.

steps: The first note has the letters tr above it: a trill.
The second has a sideways S above it: a turn.
Neither sign changes how many beats the note has.
demonstration.textAlternative: A trill and a turn above two minims.

guided.prompt: An ornament is shown by the letters tr above the note (sometimes followed by a wavy line). What is it called?

upper-mordent.reason: A trill is written tr. A mordent is a short zig-zag sign with no letters.

lower-mordent.reason: Lower mordent is shown by a short zig-zag above the note with a short vertical line through it.

turn.reason: Turn is shown by a sideways S-shaped curl above the note.

hints: Letters, a curl, a zig-zag, or a small note.
Check each detail of the description: letters or a curl, a zig-zag with or without a line, a small note with or without a stroke.

feedback.correct: Yes: you matched the name to the description.

mistakes.upper-lower-mordent-swap: Check the direction: the upper mordent goes up to the note above; the lower mordent goes down to the note below.
mistakes.turn-inverted: A turn starts on the note above; an inverted turn starts on the note below.
mistakes.acciaccatura-appoggiatura-swap: Look for the slash through the small note: with it, the note is crushed in quickly (acciaccatura); without it, it takes time from the main note (appoggiatura).
mistakes.trill-mordent-confusion: A trill keeps alternating for the length of the note; a mordent is just one quick alternation.
mistakes.ornament-confused: Check the shape of the sign: letters, a curl, a zig-zag, or a small note.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Compare the shape of the sign with each ornament's pattern.

provenance.notes: Original wording. Follows Grade 4 outcome 17 and First Steps Grade 4 section 13 (pp. 99-100, read in the PDF): the two ways of writing ornaments, the six names, no time in the bar. How the ornaments are played is Grade 5 in the book and is not asked. Notation of the mordent signs: the renderer draws the sign for each ornament name; the descriptions in words are given for accessibility.
